findings.description: Bar A's functional check yielded an unasked-for law. The covariance channel amplifies the reciprocal's relative error by K/(1-K): P' = (1-K)*P, so a relative error d in K becomes d*K/(1-K) in (1-K). Measured at P=10, R=1: amplification 10.00, observed P relative error 0.1167 against resid*amp = 0.1172, ratio 1.00. This is the application-side gain that the iterative composition theorem calls L (MonitorSoundness.lean:118), appearing in RTL rather than in a hypothesis. As K -> 1 - a confident measurement, P >> R - the amplification diverges. The theorem said the contraction constant belongs to the surrounding system; this is the surrounding system handing over its constant.

Bar D's framing partly dissolved, in the same species as bar 1. The bar asked which BIST replaces the exhaustive sweep, which presupposes the BIST still owns coverage. Under the two-instrument doctrine it does not: the BIST's job is IDENTITY, not coverage. Identity needs a witness that is deterministic, pre-committed and sensitive to datapath change - not an exhaustive one. Coverage belongs to the monitor, and the monitor reaches territory no sweep could, since bar 4's texture finding showed the good set beyond the certified domain has no interval structure. So "representative, not exhaustive" is not a concession here; it is the correct specification, and chip 1's exhaustiveness was over-provision forced by having only one instrument. Recommendation: species (i) pre-committed trajectory ROM; species (ii) REJECTED rather than deferred, because it is exhaustive over the step function - already the most trusted part, dominated by the byte-identical reciprocal - and structurally cannot exercise the recursion, which is what chip 2 adds.

chip/synth/recip.ys sets NO parameters, so it synthesises eml_reciprocal at the module defaults WIDTH=32, FRAC=16 and reports 227,174 um2 - roughly 3.4x the true 16/8 figure. That is the project's own named prior defect (defaulting the kernel's parameters, which previously read a latency of 16 where the truth is 17) sitting unnoticed inside a committed measurement script. Found only because chip 2's whole design measured SMALLER than its own sub-component, which is impossible and forced the check. A baseline that is 3.4x wrong would have made any chip-2 area comparison meaningless in the flattering direction.

Bar A measured. 6x2 fits at 60.1% utilisation with all nine setup corners positive and DRC/antenna/violations zero. Rule 22's triple reported together: Yosys 80,853.80 um2, placed standard-cell 135,595 um2, utilisation 0.600505. 4x2 would require 90.9%, above the 85% at which SWEEP_002 observed this flow fail - stated as an inference from two observations, not a measurement. The stdcell field was identified by matching chip 1's known 121,031 rather than by reading its name; design__instance__area is the CORE area and would have overstated by 67%.

The area curve finally has three points, five runs after WORST_PATH_DIAGNOSIS_001.md:104 asked for them, and the prediction that produced the request is FALSIFIED. Ratios: 1.677 at 60.1% utilisation, 1.691 at 70.9%, 1.680 at 81.1% - a 0.8% spread. The record expected the constant to vary with utilisation pressure because repair-buffer count grows as packing tightens; repair-buffer share is 11.0% versus 10.2%, so the named mechanism is real but nearly flat over this range. The third point cost one local Yosys run: chip 1's full submitted design had never had its Yosys area recorded, so its 81.1% point had no ratio at all. Validity conditions recorded per rule 22, including the one that limits it most: all three points are dominated by the same reciprocal, so the constant may be design-specific rather than flow-general, and nothing tests above 0.81.

The bar D disconfirmer FIRED and reversed the recommendation. Species (i) trajectory and species (ii) operand sweep are complementary: F1 (stuck-at on a MAC operand bit) is CAUGHT by (i) and MISSED by (ii); F2 (mis-sequence gated on z=-256, never visited by the trajectory) is MISSED by (i) and CAUGHT by (ii). A control - the same fault gated on a VISITED z - is caught by (i), which is what makes F2's escape interpretable as a blind spot rather than an inert fault. (ii) misses F1 because its fixed canonical prior gives P- = 320, which is EVEN, so clearing bit 0 of the MAC operand changes nothing: a fixed-prior sweep cannot see a fault whose visibility depends on the state VALUE. My rejection of (iii) on cost-for-value was wrong, and my named escape clause was wrong too - I claimed (ii) would also miss F2 because it resets state per operand, forgetting that it sweeps EVERY operand and therefore visits z=-256. Reasoning about one axis of a two-axis object, the same shape as bar A's 1/b-versus-saturation miss.

The pre-registered BIST criteria caught a DESIGN defect before arming: the bar A draft was a measurement update only, with no predict step, so P' = (1-K)P is monotonically non-increasing and P can never exceed P0. C1 (K>0.9) and C2 (P in the top decile) were satisfiable by ZERO of 400 trajectories, and the observed K ceiling of 0.8889 is exactly 256/(256+32) - structural, not a search artifact. Adding the predict step P- = P + Q took C1 from 0/400 to 388/400. Consequence: bar A's area and timing result was measured on an incomplete design and must be re-measured. Separately, the criteria contained an internal contradiction I wrote: C2 wanted P >= 29,490 while C5 capped S = P- + R at 4095 with S >= P-, so C2 and C5 had empty intersection on any design at this format. VOIDed as C2 with the original preserved unedited, replaced by C2' scoped to the C5-compatible range.

Bar A ANSWERED. The shared-MAC Kalman update fits 6x2 at 61.5% utilisation and meets 50 MHz at every corner, with the certified kernel byte-identical. Getting there took three hardens and the middle one failed timing: the single-cycle 16x16 multiply in the shared MAC measured max_ss -0.744 post-route, startpoint u_kf.mac_b_q[2]. Splitting the multiply (multiply|truncate, the structure eml_reciprocal uses internally) closed it: +1.16 ns for +674 um2 and three cycles. THE PATH MOVED - startpoint is now u_kf.u_recip, wholly inside the certified kernel - which is what makes it a diagnosis rather than luck, and which is precisely the terminal state HARDEN_VERDICT_006 recorded for chip 1. The kernel is byte-frozen by the cross-chip provenance claim, so this is as fast as chip 2 can be without forfeiting the identity chip 2 exists to carry.

The area-ratio band I stated from three points was too tight, and five points say so. Ratios by utilisation: 0.601->1.677, 0.612->1.704, 0.615->1.697, 0.709->1.691, 0.811->1.680. Spread 1.6%, non-monotone - the highest ratio sits at the second-lowest utilisation. The 1.68 +/- 0.01 I published after three points is falsified; 1.69 +/- 0.015 holds at five. The instructive part is the sequence: one point was promoted to a curve (phantom), three points were over-tightened into a band, and only the fourth and fifth exposed the noise floor. A constant's validity conditions are not just its regime - they are also how many points established it.

Bar B closed, and checking the "near-zero" price found it was an overestimate: the price is ZERO for the theorems themselves. 70 lines of new Lean (mostly docstring), ZERO theorems re-proved - both bodies are single applications - and one new proof of any kind, positivity of the format constant. KalmanUpdateFixedPoint.lean has no numerals in any statement or proof; every Q16.16 in it is a docstring (lines 14, 21, 67, 112, 125, 149), and s and B are free variables throughout. Q16.16 was a comment, not a hypothesis. The stronger finding is that the no-numerals architecture is enforced by the TYPE SYSTEM, not by convention: writing 1/256 fails with "failed to synthesize OfNat Real 256", because MachLib.Real has no OfNat instance for literals. A numeral cannot leak into a statement even by accident. That is why re-instantiating at a new format is a substitution rather than a project, and it retroactively justifies an architecture decision made long before chip 2 existed.

Bar C closed. B = 0.073631 (Q16.16 4825), derived from the proof and pinned by committed script sha256 39b5e676..., dual implementations agreeing. Route 2 (chained from the reciprocal's own certificate, no sweep anywhere) binds at 0.073631; route 1 (budget-inverted at eps=0.1, unit innovation) gives 0.092188. They do not disagree - route 2 is tighter, so the achievable threshold already satisfies the budget. Bar 1's pre-registered corollary is confirmed: the proof threshold is 10.9% looser than bar 4's measured worst in-domain residual, so the monitor cannot fire in the certified domain, and the measured figure appears in the script for comparison only, never entering the derivation. The honest grade: hinv0 is MEASURED NOT PROVED (no Lean file can discharge a property of a seed circuit), so chip 2's threshold is conditional on a bench measurement and no stronger than it.
